look_here_first: Think small granite spiderwort: a short narrow-leaved perennial on Llano-Uplift granitic soils, with unusually long flower pedicels and sparse glandular hairs on stems, pedicels, and sepals.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Blanco — Pedernales Falls records. Burnet — Inks Lake/Buchanan Dam records. Llano — Enchanted Rock/Llano River granite records. Mason — TPWD annotated rare-plant county list.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Restricted Llano-Uplift endemic; do not infer occurrence outside documented granitic counties.

best_field_traits: small clump-forming perennial usually 10–40 cm tall
leaf surfaces nearly glabrous to sparsely hairy
pedicels and sepals sparsely to moderately glandular-pubescent
fascicle of distally thickened tuberous roots
strong association with granite, gneiss, and derived sandy-gravelly soils
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Habitat plus stature is powerful: T. pedicellata is the small narrow-leaved granite specialist; T. edwardsiana is taller and broad-leaved; T. hirsutiflora has slender fibrous roots and favors sandy eastern-Texas habitats.
